takeaway: Pharyngeal pouch: mucosa bulges through Killian's dehiscence between thyropharyngeus and cricopharyngeus, giving a neck lump and recurrent throat symptoms.

question.text: A 73-year-old homeless man has recurrent sore throats that did not improve with antibiotics. He presents to A&E with a lump on the left side of his neck. Select the likely diagnosis.
question.say: A seventy-three-year-old homeless man has recurrent sore throats that did not improve after a course of antibiotics. He comes to A and E with a lump on the left side of his neck. What is the likely diagnosis?

answer.say: The answer is a pharyngeal pouch.

lines.text: A 73-year-old man with recurrent sore throats.
lines.say: This seventy-three-year-old man keeps getting sore throats, again and again.

lines.text: The sore throats keep coming back.
lines.say: The grey cloud of sore throat keeps circling back.
(sigh) He finished his antibiotics, but they did not help at all.

lines.text: A lump on the left of his neck.
lines.say: Now he points to a lump on the left side of his neck.

lines.text: The inferior constrictor has two parts: thyropharyngeus above, cricopharyngeus below.
lines.say: Here is why. The inferior constrictor has two parts, thyropharyngeus above and cricopharyngeus below.

lines.text: Mucosa bulges through the gap: Killian's dehiscence.
lines.say: Between them is a weak gap, Killian's dehiscence. The mucosa pouches out through it.

lines.text: Remember: a neck lump with stubborn throat symptoms is a pharyngeal pouch.
lines.say: Remember: an older patient with a neck lump and stubborn throat symptoms has a pharyngeal pouch.
